# uncertainty-vst-2026

> Code for "Probabilistic uncertainty in virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology is largely redundant with the predicted mean" (Batique, Nonchev, Koelzer and Rätsch, bioRxiv 2026). A systematic benchmark of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty for spot-level gene expression predicted from H&E histology images on 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics.

## Key Facts

- Benchmarks predictive uncertainty for virtual spatial transcriptomics, i.e. gene expression predicted from H&E histology
- Three 10x Visium cancer cohorts, 60 sections: metastatic melanoma (Tumor Profiler), kidney and lung tumors with tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS), and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); 3,000 highly variable genes; leave-one-patient-out cross-validation
- Frozen H&E encoder: Midnight (kaiko-ai/midnight); an MLP maps patch embeddings to the parameters of a predictive distribution
- Aleatoric uncertainty: Gaussian (heteroscedastic, gene- and spot-homoscedastic, beta-NLL), Poisson and negative binomial heads, plus the STimage readout
- Epistemic uncertainty: deep ensembles, MC dropout, last-layer Laplace approximation
- Baselines: a histology-free per-gene marginal, a training-free kNN neighborhood signal, an error oracle
- Evaluation: PIT calibration, and error informativeness via partial Spearman correlation controlling for the predicted mean and sparsification curves against the oracle; computed per (slide, gene), then averaged
- Main finding: uncertainty is associated with prediction error, but the predicted mean largely explains that association; after accounting for the mean, uncertainty carries only weak information about larger errors. Good calibration does not imply informative uncertainty: simple distributions fitted without histology are calibrated too
- Snakemake pipeline (SLURM profile), PyTorch, MIT licensed

## When to Use This Repository

- You want to check whether the uncertainty of your own histology-to-gene-expression model is calibrated and informative beyond its predicted mean: `notebooks/reproducing_the_numbers_on_any_predictions.ipynb` computes every metric of the paper from any predictions
- You need implementations of PIT calibration, partial Spearman informativeness or sparsification curves for spatial transcriptomics (`src/evaluation/`)
- You want to reproduce the benchmark of the paper

## Related Projects

- [DeepSpot](https://github.com/ratschlab/DeepSpot): Predicts spatial transcriptomics from H&E images, at spot-level (Visium) and single-cell (Xenium) resolution
- [DeepSpot-M](https://github.com/ratschlab/DeepSpotM): Multimodal foundation model for transcriptome-wide virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology
- [DeepSpot2Cell](https://github.com/ratschlab/DeepSpot2Cell): Predicts virtual single-cell spatial transcriptomics from H&E images
- [Aurora](https://www.auroraomics.org): No-code platform for virtual spatial transcriptomics from H&E images

## Installation

```
git clone https://github.com/ratschlab/uncertainty-vst-2026
cd uncertainty-vst-2026
conda env create -f environment_mtenv0_minimal.yml
conda activate mtenv0
pip install -e .
```

## Quick Start

Set the `/path/to/...` placeholders in `snake/config/config.yaml`, then run the main sweep:

```
snakemake --snakefile snake/Snakefile --configfile snake/config/config.yaml \
  --profile snake/profile all_classic
```

## Citation

Batique, T., Nonchev, K., Koelzer, V.H. and Rätsch, G. (2026). Probabilistic uncertainty in virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology is largely redundant with the predicted mean. bioRxiv. DOI: 10.64898/2026.10.23.760875
